# ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops Daily Update (Jun 19, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's activity focused on addressing a critical flake in `reth-optimism-node` integration tests and clarifying an issue with intrinsic gas on Optimism Sepolia after the Karst hard fork. A new pull request was opened to require signatures for execution.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
A new pull request, [#1477](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1477), was opened to require signatures for execution.

## CLOSED ISSUES

## NEW ISSUES

## ACTIVE ISSUES
### Addressing `reth-optimism-node` Integration Test Flake
Discussion on [#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/20973) confirms that the `reth-optimism-node` integration test `peers_negotiate_eth_69` continues to experience a `SIGSEGV` on teardown. A recent recurrence of this flake kicked a separate pull request out of the merge queue, highlighting its ongoing impact. The issue is suspected to be related to how the payload builder service handles `std::thread` and `tokio` runtime teardown, potentially leading to a race condition when accessing freed `tokio` internals.

### Optimism Sepolia Intrinsic Gas Issue
The issue [#21457](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/21457) regarding high intrinsic gas on Optimism Sepolia after the Karst hard fork was acknowledged as a known issue. It is expected to be resolved in the next release, as indicated in the Optimism upgrade notices.

### `op-reth` Metrics Version Discrepancy
Issue [#20832](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/20832) highlights a discrepancy in the version reported by `op-reth` in Prometheus metrics, `web3_clientVersion`, and `--version` flag. The current version is populated from `Cargo.toml`, but the desired behavior is for it to correspond to the git tag that triggered the build, similar to the Go stack.
